data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The nocturnal UHI is an emergent surface-energy-budget disequilibrium: the single governing mechanism is the relaxation timescale of stored sensible heat in the urban fabric, which integrates heat capacity, imperviousness, sky view, and anthropogenic heat into one lag term; the cross-city gap scales with this thermal relaxation timescale, which increases with thermal mass, impervious surface fraction, and building height, and decreases with sky view and wind speed.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the nocturnal cooling of urban air were found to follow an exponential relaxation with a timescale independent of thermal mass, this mechanism would be overturned.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the cross-city UHI intensity did not scale with any measure of thermal relaxation time, the unification would fail.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If wind speed and sky view factor manipulated independently produced cooling rates inconsistent with a single relaxation timescale, this mechanism would be weakened.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The surface energy budget forces a relaxation timescale: dT/dt \u221d -(T_urban - T_equilibrium)/\u03c4, where \u03c4 is the thermal relaxation time of the urban canopy. A longer \u03c4 means urban air cools more slowly, widening the nighttime gap relative to fast-cooling countryside. \u03c4 increases with heat capacity and thermal mass of impervious materials, is modulated by reduced sky view (slower radiative loss), and decreases with wind speed (faster advective removal). Anthropogenic heat adds a forcing term that sustains the disequilibrium. The cross-city gap scales with \u03c4, making it the single unifying mechanism.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
